findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix so AMS never calls it
findings.body: ActiveModelSerializers 0.8/0.9 (used by Discourse) only honors filter methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `def include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is never invoked and `website_name` is always serialized — including when `website` is blank, in which case `website_name` returns nil and clients see an explicit `website_name: null`. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name leaks the website domain for TL0 users seen by anonymous visitors
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list hides `website` (and other profile fields) from anonymous viewers of trust-level-0 users, but the new `website_name` attribute was not added to that list and has no `restrict_user_fields?` guard. As a result, an anonymous crawler can still read the domain (or full host+path) of a TL0 user's website via `website_name` even though `website` itself is suppressed, defeating the purpose of the restriction. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` or gate its inclusion on `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`.

findings.title: website_name returns nil for URLs without a scheme
findings.body: `URI(website.to_s).host` returns nil for scheme-less websites like `example.com/user` (which Discourse accepts and displays). The method then returns nil even though `website` is present, so the profile shows no website name at all for those users. Previously the client-side `website.split("/")[2]` had similar limitations, but the new server-side code should normalize the URL (e.g. prepend `http://` when no scheme) before parsing instead of silently returning nil.

findings.title: Second-level-domain comparison treats unrelated subdomains as the same site
findings.body: The branch comparing `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]` treats e.g. website `www.wordpress.com` and instance `forum.wordpress.com` (or any two customers of a shared hosting domain) as the same site and exposes the full URL path. The old behavior only showed the host; this change reveals path information for domains that merely share a suffix. Consider using an exact-suffix check (`website_host == discourse_host || website_host.ends_with?('.' + discourse_host) || discourse_host.ends_with?('.' + website_host)`) instead of comparing truncated labels, which also mishandles multi-part TLDs like `example.co.uk`.
